subject: MAP: anchoring the close date — proposed bridge and procurement checkpoints

Subject: MAP: anchoring the close date — proposed bridge and procurement checkpoints

Sara —

Following our sync this morning, attaching a focused MAP and a procurement checklist that target the items MediCore called out. High level proposal:

- Re-baseline close to 2026-09-24 (three-week buffer) to allow procurement PO, SOC evidence dispatch, and a one-week acceptance canary.
- Bridge items (must-have): signed PO, SOC 2 evidence package (we can provide the redacted bundle by EOD Mon), Docusign for the addendum, and a scoped canary acceptance plan.
- Risk delta: procurement lag and internal security review — mitigations below.

Immediate asks:
1) Please confirm whether MediCore can commit to a PO by 2026-09-10.
2) Confirm acceptance criteria owner (who signs off on canary) and a functional contact for the week of 9/20.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v3.pdf (application/pdf, 96 KB); procurement-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42 KB)

Proposed owners (short):
- Redwood: Markus (deal owner), Camila (solutions lead)
- MediCore: Sara (procurement lead), Procurement Team (legal/PO)

If you prefer a shorter re-baseline (2 weeks) we can accelerate the SOC evidence hand-off and prioritize the canary, but that will reduce the acceptance window.

Thanks,

Markus Klein

Thanks for the clear proposal. MediCore is under procurement review this quarter; our internal PO cadence is tight but not impossible. A few clarifying points:

- We can aim to issue a PO by 2026-09-12 if the SOC evidence and the addendum are complete this week. Can you confirm the earliest you can send the redacted SOC bundle?
- For the canary acceptance, our security reviewer (Tom R.) needs a one-week window to run smoke tests against a bounded dataset. Is a 5-business-day canary feasible?

Subject: Re: MAP: anchoring the close date — proposed bridge and procurement checkpoints

Sara —

We can support a 5-business-day canary. Proposed acceptance plan (summary):

- Day 0: Canary deploy to Dedicated test pool (isolated tenant), run synthetic traffic and ingestion with the supplied sample dataset.
- Day 1–3: Tom’s team to run functional + security smoke tests; Camila to run perf and token-cost validation.
- Day 4: Joint acceptance run and sign-off window; fallback to snapshot and rerun if criteria fail.

Technical notes / mitigations:
- We will enable prefix KV caching and a temporary 2X request rate limit to ensure deterministic latency during the canary.
- If latency variance appears, we will drop to a lower-capacity instance type for the canary while we stabilize kernels — this preserves determinism but increases unit cost (Ben — see cost note below).

Attached: eval-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18 KB)

Action items for procurement: please confirm the functional contact for sign-off and whether Tom can be granted a test account with limited data.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Solutions Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Confirmed: we can reserve a dedicated test pool for the MediCore canary the week of 2026-09-20. Two notes:

1) SLA exception: to guarantee low-latency determinism during the canary we recommend the optional SLA uplift addendum — this adds a 5% surcharge but avoids preemption risk.
2) Cost impact: dedicated-test pool for a 5-business-day canary + increased kernel stability ops is estimated at ~$2.6k (one-time). If procurement wants escrow/credit triggers, we can add a time-boxed remediation credit line in the addendum.

Sara / Team —

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Per the above thread we have agreement on the following immediate MAP updates and next steps:

1) Re-baseline close to 2026-09-24 (target go-live window for production cutover 9/24–9/27).
2) MediCore to issue PO by 2026-09-12. Procurement to confirm PO format by EOD Wed (procurement@medicore.com).
3) Redwood to deliver redacted SOC 2 evidence package by 2026-08-31 (we will send via secure link).
4) Canary acceptance: 5 business days during week of 9/20 — Redwood will provision a dedicated test pool and enable deterministic config (Ben to provision).
5) Escrow / credit: Ben to include a time-boxed remediation credit in the addendum; procurement to confirm acceptable trigger language.

Risk log (short):
- Risk #1: Procurement lag -> Impact: close slip -> Mitigation: PO target 9/12 + executive escalations if missed. Owner: MediCore procurement.
- Risk #2: Canary fails functional tests -> Impact: 1–2 week delay -> Mitigation: remediation credit + rerun window; Redwood to snapshot and provide replay. Owner: Camila/Redwood.
- Risk #3: SOC evidence delay -> Impact: procurement hold -> Mitigation: partial redacted bundle + legal attestation; Owner: Markus/Redwood.

Next meetings:
- Procurement checklist review (30 min) — Thu 2026-09-02 10:00 AM ET — invite pending.
- Canary run kickoff — Mon 2026-09-20 09:00 AM PT.

Links: HubSpot record https://hubspot.example/contacts/DEAL-7841; DocuSign envelope https://docusign.example/envelope/0f8b2a

I’ll circulate an updated MAP (v4) after we get procurement PO format. Thanks all — we’ll treat the 9/24 target as the anchored date unless we see a hard blocker.

Best,
